title: Paloma and the Signal
premise: Jude Sandoval is a clone of a murdered dockworker, legally erased and hauling cargo through contested orbits to stay invisible. When the manifest of the Meridian Grace—a ship that officially never flew—lists a name only Jude's original would recognize, he follows it into a conspiracy to erase the Kestrel Yard massacre that killed his source. With help from Paloma Reyes, a records-archivist turned smuggler who remembers what the archives were made to forget, Jude gathers testimony from survivors the state insists are dead. The climax comes at the jump window: Jude broadcasts the massacre evidence through the contested relay as corporate enforcers close in, sacrificing his anonymity forever. In the end, justice arrives not as a verdict but as memory—the names restored to the record, with Jude choosing to sign his own.
about_author: Odile Lockridge is the pen name of a former maritime logistics analyst who spent a decade writing shipping manifests before turning them into fiction. She writes near-future thrillers about people the paperwork was designed to erase.

chapters.title: Dead Weight
chapters.summary: Jude Sandoval hauls refrigerated cargo through the contested Verge orbits, keeping his head down and his clone status buried. A routine inspection nearly exposes him. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: the exhausting vigilance of a man whose existence is technically illegal.

chapters.title: The Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: A broker offers Jude a lucrative run on the Meridian Grace—but registry checks show the ship was scrapped eleven years ago, and its manifest lists 'E. Sandoval,' his murdered original. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: dread curdling into compulsion; someone knows what he is.

chapters.title: Paloma
chapters.summary: Tracking the manifest anomaly, Jude finds Paloma Reyes, an ex-archivist running black-market record restoration out of a decommissioned station chapel. She confirms the Meridian Grace carried witnesses out of Kestrel Yard. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: wary alliance between two people who deal in forbidden truths.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Paloma shows Jude her hidden archive: fragments proving the Kestrel Yard massacre happened—payroll gaps, deleted manifests, a survivor's voice recording. Corporate consortium Halcyon Orbital rewrote everything. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: grief transformed into purpose; Jude confronting his original's death for the first time.

chapters.title: Survivors of Record
chapters.summary: Jude and Paloma locate one living witness, Ilsa Vann, hiding under a false identity in the Verge. Her testimony is damning but she refuses to speak unless her family is protected. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: the weight of asking others to risk what he's spent years avoiding.

chapters.title: Manifest Interest
chapters.summary: Halcyon's fixer, Corvane, traces the manifest query back toward Paloma's station. Jude buys time with a decoy cargo run while Ilsa agrees to testify—if they can get her off-station before the quarterly jump window closes. POV: alternating Jude/Paloma. Emotional beat: the clock starts; paranoia sharpens into resolve.

chapters.title: The Long Silence
chapters.summary: En route to the jump relay, Corvane's enforcers board and seize their cargo, and Ilsa is taken. Jude must choose: flee invisible or use his clone status as legal grounds to demand a hearing no court will grant. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: rock bottom—the price of survival has always been silence, and he's done paying it.

chapters.title: Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Paloma reveals her last card: a dormant broadcast node inside the jump relay itself, built by archivists like her. They plan to hijack the window when all Verge traffic syncs to it. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: terrified hope; two outsiders betting everything on infrastructure meant to be forgotten.

chapters.title: The Jump Window
chapters.summary: Climax. As the window opens, Jude infiltrates the relay station to free Ilsa while Paloma loads the massacre archive into the broadcast. Corvane corners Jude, but Jude's testimony—his own inherited memory of E. Sandoval's final hours—goes out with everything else. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: catharsis through exposure; invisibility traded for truth.

chapters.title: Names Restored
chapters.summary: The broadcast spreads through the Verge faster than Halcyon can suppress it. Investigations reopen; survivors emerge claiming their names. Jude, now publicly known, signs the restored memorial ledger as both Sandovals—and chooses to keep flying, visible at last. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won peace; inheritance reclaimed as identity rather than debt.
